items.title: fix: distinguish session groups from the create action (#156822)
items.summary: fix: distinguish session groups from the create action (#156822) Related: #142863 Replaces #153883; the original stays open until this fix lands. ## What Problem This Solves Selecting an existing session group named `__new-group__` opens New Group instead of assigning the session to that group. ## User Impact All group names behave as data. New Group, ordinary assignment, drag-and-drop and denied-write behavior stay intact. No appearance, permission, schema or RPC changes. ## Why This Change Was Made Mark the create option explicitly and inspect the selected option rather than reserving a group-name string. Keep the current `category-cell.ts` owner and its existing DOM guard; do not restore the earlier extraction. The two category tests move out of the oversized view test file without losing assertions, adding a colliding-name case and a positive create-action control. Production shrinks by two lines; three files total, +120/−104. ## Evidence - On main `764c9331a31`, the real Sessions renderer regression failed for `__new-group__` while two controls passed. With the fix, all three category cases and all 51 remaining view cases pass. - Per-file `pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`: category suite 2.25s wall (collision 17ms); remaining view suite 2.64s wall. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35928486234): category test execution 0.128s (collision 48ms); remaining view tests 1.087s. - Fresh canonical changed checks passed (format, lint, typegraphs, line/assertion guards and dead exports). Independent P0–P2 review: scoped-clean, no findings. Current-head ClawSweeper review completed with no findings. Exact-head hosted CI remains enforced for landing. - Behavior-only DOM boundary proof; no live Gateway or screenshot evidence is claimed. Replacement provenance and earlier CI limitation The original PR could not be safely rebased through the native ancestry-preserving publisher. Its accepted auto-merge was cancelled through native retained-outcome recovery before this authorized replacement was started from current main. No old receipt or guard was removed. The old head’s [Node small-18 failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35830173387/job/107080979527) reported forced rather than cooperative SIGINT cleanup. Matching-runtime investigation did not reproduce it; that is not a verified fix or proof of flakiness. The older extraction also had a separate Node dispatch failure and 2-byte startup diagnostic. This replacement includes no process-code or budget changes, and neither old passing checks nor nonreproduction qualify its new head. Earlier diagnostics remain in the original PR. Continues the work requested by @vyctorbrzezowski, preserving credit to @vyctorbrzezowski, @steipete, @fuller-stack-dev, @vincentkoc and @shakkernerd. ## Work sessions - [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/28feaf46-a23c-468e-bfad-ab44a1d5ac7b) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/949fe0ab-0f88-4056-a482-913b7f4974f4) Co-authored-by: vyctorbrzezowski Co-authored-by: steipete Co-authored-by: fuller-stack-dev Co-authored-by: vincentkoc Co-authored-by: shakkernerd
